samples.summary: No test covers a cell that carries non-border style when a border preset is applied/cleared
samples.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4009-4020) merges the patch into the existing `cell.s` and then deletes only the patched keys, i.e. it is specifically responsible for PRESERVING unrelated style keys (`b`, `al`, `bg`, ...) across a border apply/clear. Every new and updated test in the diff starts from a cell with either no style at all (lines 272-342, 361-367) or with only a value (`{ v: 'Label' }`, lines 344-359), so no assertion would fail if the merge dropped or clobbered an existing non-border style. A test like `setStyle({b:true})` -> `setRangeBorders('all')` -> `setRangeBorders('clear')` expecting `{b:true}` to survive is absent.

samples.summary: Explicit-`false` retention is only tested for the column-style layer, not row/sheet/range-style layers
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:3990-3991) claims a `false` needed to override a 'sheet/column/row/range-style layer' is still written, but only the column case is exercised ('should keep an explicit false when a column border needs overriding', selectColumn(1) + setRangeStyle({bt:true})). No test drives the sheet-wide, row, or explicit range-style source through `pruneRedundantDefaultStyleKeys`/`hasConflictingStyleSourceForKey` from the border path, so a regression in how `getStyleSources()` feeds those layers into the border path would go unnoticed.

samples.summary: The new no-op short-circuits (`!prev && !style`, `stylesEqual(prev, style)`) have no test that proves no write happens
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:4022-4027 adds two early returns whose whole purpose is to avoid storing/deleting an identical payload. The tests only check the resulting style via `getStyle`/`fetchGrid`, which look identical whether the short-circuit fires or an identical payload is rewritten (or a delete is issued). No test spies on the store (e.g. MemStore set/delete counts) or checks a version/change flag, so removing either guard would keep the suite green. Nothing in the diff or in formatting.test.ts asserts write suppression.
searchedFor: grep setRangeBorders repo-wide for store-spy style tests

finding.summary: No test covers a cell that carries non-border style when a border preset is applied/cleared
finding.evidence: `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:4009-4020) merges the patch into the existing `cell.s` and then deletes only the patched keys, i.e. it is specifically responsible for PRESERVING unrelated style keys (`b`, `al`, `bg`, ...) across a border apply/clear. Every new and updated test in the diff starts from a cell with either no style at all (lines 272-342, 361-367) or with only a value (`{ v: 'Label' }`, lines 344-359), so no assertion would fail if the merge dropped or clobbered an existing non-border style. A test like `setStyle({b:true})` -> `setRangeBorders('all')` -> `setRangeBorders('clear')` expecting `{b:true}` to survive is absent.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `applyBorderPatch` (sheet.ts:3993-4035) merges the border patch into `cell.s` and then deletes only the patched keys, so preserving unrelated style keys is a property it is specifically responsible for — the task doc asserts it explicitly ("Only the keys the border patch touched are considered, so unrelated cell style is left alone", todo.md:32-35). Repo-wide grep shows the ONLY test caller of `setRangeBorders`/`applyBorders` anywhere is packages/sheets/test/sheet/formatting.test.ts; the frontend caller (formatting-toolbar.tsx:272) and view wrapper (spreadsheet.ts:242) have no tests, and there are no e2e tests touching borders. Reading the whole border block (formatting.test.ts:272-492), every case starts from an empty cell (272, 302, 330, 361, 380), a value-only cell `{v:'Label'}` (344-350), or a border-only inherited style `setRangeStyle({bt:true})` (369-378). No test seeds a non-border key (b/i/bg/al/nf) before applying or clearing a preset, so a merge that dropped or clobbered existing non-border style would not fail any assertion. The nearest test (line 344 round trip) only proves the cell *value* survives via compactCell, not any style key.
